summary: Describes route reflection, a method that reduces the need for a full mesh of internal BGP sessions inside a network. It is a standards-track document at the proposed standard level, and it was replaced by RFC 4456.

eli5.summary: Instead of everyone talking to everyone, one helper gathers the news and passes it on to the rest.

questions: how to avoid full mesh ibgp
subtitle: Reducing the BGP configuration burden by having one router relay routes to others.

tldr.problem: In a BGP autonomous system with many internal routers, all routers must exchange routes with every other router in a full mesh. For n routers, this requires n*(n-1)/2 sessions, which becomes unmanageable as networks grow.
tldr.mechanism: Route Reflection allows one router (the Route Reflector) to advertise IBGP-learned routes to other internal peers, relaxing the rule that IBGP speakers don't re-advertise internal routes. This eliminates the need for many direct connections.
tldr.outcome: Networks can organize internal routers into clusters served by one or more reflectors, reducing configuration complexity and improving scalability. RFC 4456 is the updated specification.

today: RFC 2796 describes route reflection as a Proposed Standard and is a revision of RFC 1966. It was replaced by RFC 4456, which provides the current specification.

sections.title: The Full Mesh Problem
sections.content:
The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is used for routing across the Internet and within large networks. In a single autonomous system, all BGP speakers must exchange external routing information with each other using internal BGP (IBGP).

With current BGP rules, every internal router must form a direct IBGP session with every other internal router in the autonomous system—a full mesh. For a network with n routers, this requires n*(n-1)/2 unique IBGP sessions. A network with 100 internal routers would need 4,950 sessions, which is difficult to configure and manage. Route Reflection solves this by allowing one router to advertise learned routes to peers.
sections.eli5: If 100 people all need to know what's happening, one way is for each person to talk directly to all the others. That takes a lot of conversations. A better way is for a few people to listen and then tell the rest.

sections.title: Route Reflection Concepts
sections.content:
A Route Reflector is a BGP speaker configured to advertise IBGP-learned routes to certain IBGP peers, normally not allowed in IBGP. A route reflector has two types of internal peers: Client Peers (which need not be fully meshed) and Non-Client Peers (which must be fully meshed with each other).

A Route Reflector and its client peers form a Cluster. Within a cluster, clients only need IBGP sessions to the route reflector, not to each other. Multiple route reflectors can serve different clusters, and the reflectors themselves must be fully meshed. This reduces the total number of sessions from n*(n-1)/2 to roughly n plus the number of clusters.
sections.eli5: The clusters are like small teams with a team leader (the reflector) who talks to everyone. The team members only need to talk to their leader, not to each other.

sections.title: How Routes Are Reflected
sections.content:
When a Route Reflector receives a route from an IBGP peer, it selects the best path using its normal path selection rules. Then it reflects that route depending on the peer type: if the route comes from a Non-Client peer, it is reflected to all clients; if from a Client peer, it is reflected to both Non-Client peers and all other Client peers. This ensures all routers in the domain eventually see external routes.

A Route Reflector treats other Route Reflectors as normal IBGP speakers and can be configured to have them as either Client or Non-Client peers. This allows for hierarchical architectures where multiple clusters exchange routes through reflectors, and conventional BGP speakers that don't understand route reflection can coexist in the network.
sections.eli5: When a reflector hears important news, it passes it on to everyone who needs to know, depending on who told it the news and what role they have.

sections.title: Preventing Routing Loops
sections.content:
Route Reflection introduces two new BGP attributes to prevent routing loops. The ORIGINATOR_ID attribute carries the router ID of the route originator. A router should ignore any route where the ORIGINATOR_ID matches its own router ID, preventing loops when a route travels back to its source.

The CLUSTER_LIST attribute records the sequence of route reflector cluster IDs that a route has passed through. When a route reflector reflects a route, it prepends its CLUSTER_ID to the list. If a router receives a route with its own CLUSTER_ID in the CLUSTER_LIST, it discards the route, preventing loops caused by misconfiguration within clusters.
sections.eli5: Every route has a tag saying who originally sent it and which clusters it has visited. If a route comes back to the same cluster, routers ignore it so it doesn't loop forever.

sections.title: Deployment and Considerations
sections.content:
A client peer cannot dynamically identify itself to a route reflector; configuration is required. The primary benefit of route reflection is that the reflector summarizes routing information and reflects only the best path, reducing the amount of data exchanged.

Deployment must account for the fact that route reflectors may make different best-path selections than a full-mesh topology due to different IGP metrics or MED values between clusters. A common approach is point-of-presence (POP) based reflection, where each POP has its own route reflectors fully meshed with each other, and clients in each POP are fully meshed to achieve consistent routing within the POP. This ensures routing behavior remains predictable and consistent.
sections.eli5: Setting up reflectors requires careful planning so that routers in different places make similar routing decisions and no traffic gets lost or misrouted due to how the clusters are arranged.

left.title: Full Mesh IBGP
left.desc: Each router connects directly to all others. Scales as n*(n-1)/2 sessions.

right.title: Route Reflection
right.desc: Clients connect to reflector only, reflectors connect to each other. Much fewer sessions.
